questions.stem: A surveyor walks 49 km south, turns left and walks 60 km, then turns left and walks 4 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 75. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 45 km along the initial direction and 60 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(45² + 60²) = 75 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 74 km west, turns left and walks 144 km, then turns left and walks 14 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 156. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 60 km along the initial direction and 144 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(60² + 144²) = 156 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 49 km east, turns right and walks 72 km, then turns right and walks 19 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 78. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 30 km along the initial direction and 72 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(30² + 72²) = 78 km.

questions.stem: In a queue of 53 candidates, a candidate is 17th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 34. New front rank = 17+3 = 20. Back rank = 53 − 20 + 1 = 34.

questions.stem:
Statements: X = P > R = U = V.
Conclusions: I. X ≥ V   II. U ≤ V.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem: E is the brother of A. A is the mother of H. F is the father of E and A. How is E related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. E is the brother of H’s mother A. Therefore E is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: B is the only daughter of G. G is the father of B. A is the son of B. H is the sister of G. How is G related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. G is the father of B, and B is A’s mother. Thus G is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: C is the mother of G. D is the daughter of G. F is the father of G. How is D related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. F is a parent of G, and D is G’s daughter. Hence D is F’s grandchild.

rural savings banking = vo re ka
growth savings secure = lu ni vo
access banking secure = re mi lu

questions.stem: A boat covers 96 km in still water in 6 hours. If the stream flows at 3 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 3 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 39. Still-water speed = 16 km/h. Upstream speed = 16 − 3. Distance = speed × 3.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 14 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 42. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+14)/(x+14) = 3/2 gives x = 14. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem:
I. x² − 14x + 48 = 0
II. y² − 6y + 8 = 0
Choose the strongest relationship that holds for all possible root pairings.
options: x = y or relationship cannot be determined
questions.explanation: Answer: x > y. Factor I: roots 6, 8. Factor II: roots 2, 4. Compare all four pairings to obtain x > y.

questions.stem: A 190 m train moving at 86.4 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 14.4 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 9.5. Relative speed = (86.4 − 14.4) ×5/18 = 20 m/s. Time = 190/20.

questions.stem: A container holds 90 litres of pure milk. 18 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 57.6. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 90 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: [Caselet set] What is the average number in the female category across A, C and E? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 693.33. Derived data: A: first category 1140, second category 760; B: first category 360, second category 480; C: first category 360, second category 540; D: first category 780, second category 520; E: first category 1300, second category 780. (760 + 540 + 780) ÷ 3.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] The combined total at A and D is what percentage more or less than the total at C? Give the absolute percentage difference, rounded to two decimals.
questions.explanation: Answer: 255.56. Derived data: A: first category 1140, second category 760; B: first category 360, second category 480; C: first category 360, second category 540; D: first category 780, second category 520; E: first category 1300, second category 780. Percentage difference = |total(A)+total(D)−total(C)| ÷ total(C) × 100.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] If 25% of the female category at E is transferred to the male category there, what is the new size of the male category at E?
questions.explanation: Answer: 1495. Derived data: A: first category 1140, second category 760; B: first category 360, second category 480; C: first category 360, second category 540; D: first category 780, second category 520; E: first category 1300, second category 780. New first category = 1300 + 25% of 780.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] The female category at D is what percentage of the male category at B? (Round to two decimal places.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 144.44. Derived data: A: first category 1140, second category 760; B: first category 360, second category 480; C: first category 360, second category 540; D: first category 780, second category 520; E: first category 1300, second category 780. 520 ÷ 360 × 100 = 144.44%.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] If the male category at C increases by 20% and the female category there decreases by 10%, what is the new total?
questions.explanation: Answer: 918. Derived data: A: first category 1140, second category 760; B: first category 360, second category 480; C: first category 360, second category 540; D: first category 780, second category 520; E: first category 1300, second category 780. 360 × 1.20 + 540 × 0.90.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 38 and 57 hours. An outlet empties it in 114 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 28.5. Net rate = 1/38 + 1/57 − 1/114 = 2/57 tank/hour. Required time = 28.5 hours.
